title: Digging Safely Around Buried Utilities
summary: Hitting a buried gas line, power cable, or other utility can cause explosions, electrocution, and death. This talk covers locating, verifying, and hand-digging near marked lines.
talking_points: Before digging, confirm with your supervisor that utility companies were notified and all lines are marked. On public land with no markings, call 811.
On private property, ask the supervisor or owner to bring in a private utility locating service before you dig.
Know the color code: red marks electrical lines, yellow marks gas lines. Look for paint, flags, or stakes.
Treat mark-outs as approximate. Dig by hand within 2 feet of any mark-out. If markings are unclear, stop and verify with the utility company.
While digging, watch for signs of past digging, changes in soil, asphalt patches, depressions, or buried concrete, plastic, or gravel.
If you hit a line, report it right away. For a gas line, evacuate everyone, secure the area, and call the fire department and gas utility.
site_hazards_to_check: No utility markings, or markings that do not match the dig plan
Heavy equipment digging within 2 feet of a mark-out instead of hand digging
Signs of previous excavation: soil color changes, asphalt patches, or depressions
Exposed or nicked conduit, cable, or pipe in the excavation
No evacuation or emergency plan if a gas line is struck
discussion_questions: Which utilities are marked in our dig area today, and what do the colors mean?
How close to a mark-out can we use the machine before we switch to hand digging?
What is the plan if someone hits a gas line?

flags: RESOLVED: 29 CFR 1926.1408 (cranes/equipment near overhead lines) has been removed - it did not fit a buried-utility talk.

RESOLVED: 29 CFR 1926.416(a)(1) added - correct for the struck-energized-line electrocution hazard (no employee may work where they could contact an electric power circuit unless it is de-energized and grounded or effectively guarded).

VERIFIED: 1926.651 (underground installations at 651(b) - determine location before opening, notify utilities / the one-call/811 system, protect and support exposed lines, and excavate by safe/acceptable means near the estimated location) and 1926.652 (protective systems) are correctly cited and match the talking points.

TOLERANCE NOTE (not a defect): the 'hand-dig within 2 feet of a mark-out' figure is a state/one-call tolerance-zone convention (commonly 18-24 in), not a federal number; 1926.651(b)(4) requires safe and acceptable means (generally hand excavation) when approaching the estimated location. Acceptable as practice guidance. APWA color code (red = electric, yellow = gas) is stated correctly.
